newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy anti-trust body probes natural gas companies.
newsitem.headline: Italy anti-trust body probes natural gas companies.

text.p: Italy's anti-trust watchdog said on Tuesday it was investigating certain activities of Snam, the natural gas unit of energy group ENI, and Societa Gasdotti del Mezzogiorno SpA (SGM), a unit of Edison Gas.
The watchdog said in a statement that its action followed a complaint by an industry body near the southern town of Campobasso.
It said it was looking into possible concerted action in regions where the activities of the two companies overlapped and a possible abuse of a dominant position in the natural gas market by SGM.

Snam is 96 percent owned by ENI and has a methane pipeline network of some 25,000 km. SGM, which transports and sells natural gas in Lazio, around Rome and Molise, Campania and Puglia in southern Italy, has a network of some 600 km.

The anti-trust authority, chaired by former prime minister Giuliano Amato, said concerted action between Snam and SGM, whereby Snam agreed not to operate in competition with SGM in areas where both groups operated pipelines and SGM undertook to offer users the same conditions as Snam, "cannot be ruled out".

It said that as a result of such an agreement, SGM would be in a dominant position, able to act independently of other competitors, and would have abused that position by refusing to link an industrial consortium to its network.
The consortium brought the complaint which triggered the anti-trust inquiry.

That consortium had built a methane pipeline to bring gas to its companies and had asked to be linked to SGM's network. SGM said this could only happen if it were granted management and direct supply of the firms' gas requirements.

The consortium rejected SGM's terms and brought in another company to manage gas supply, but SGM refused to supply gas saying it was not commercial practice to have a third party between the supplier and end user.
The consortium then turned to Snam, which also operates a pipeline in the area, but received no reply by the time it brought its formal complaint earlier this month.

"It therefore appears that Snam does not represent an effective competitor to SGM and that SGM is thus the only methane gas supplier for industrial use in the Campobasso Boiano region," the anti-trust watchdog said.
